title: Form and emptiness
hookLine: form is emptiness, emptiness is form (Heart Sutra)
tomorrow: the sutra ends on a mantra. what does 'gate gate' actually say?

cards: A coffee cup on the counter, still warm. Is it empty or full? The Heart Sutra says the answer is stranger than either.
In the longer telling, the Buddha sits on Vulture Peak, deep in meditation, and Shariputra asks Avalokiteshvara how to practice perfect wisdom.

The answer is the line at the sutra's center: form is emptiness, emptiness is form. Emptiness is not other than form; form is not other than emptiness. When he finishes, the Buddha rises and says: well said, well said.

teach.h: EMPTY OF A SELF OF ITS OWN.
teach.b: Here's the question, and the Mahayana answer. What does empty mean? Not that the cup isn't there.
It's there: that's form. Empty means empty of a self of its own.
The cup is clay, fire, a potter's hands, water, a truck, your hand reaching for it. Take those away and there's no cup left over.

This is the teaching of shunyata, emptiness, and the teacher Nagarjuna tied it to the Buddha's teaching that everything arises from causes. Whatever arises that way, he says, is what we call emptiness.

So emptiness is not a void behind things. It's how things are: open, connected, changing. The teacher Thich Nhat Hanh put it his own way: look closely at a sheet of paper and you'll find the cloud that rained on the tree.

Now a neighbor who also loves an empty cup. The Tao Te Ching, the book tradition credits to Laozi, in James Legge's words: "Clay is fashioned into vessels; but it is on their empty hollowness, that their use depends."
Shared: both refuse to call empty worthless.
The honest difference: for the Tao Te Ching, the emptiness is the useful space inside the cup.
For the Heart Sutra, the cup itself, clay and all, is empty of a separate self, through and through. Two old answers to one cup.

how: Mahayana Buddhists chant 'form is emptiness, emptiness is form' as part of the Heart Sutra, and study emptiness through teachers such as Nagarjuna; Taoists read the Tao Te Ching's empty vessel in their own way.

o: everything is real yet has no self of its own
a mind wiped clean of every single thought
nothing exists at all; the world is a dream

games.q: the cup, two ways: tap the pairs.
p: what arises from causes is emptiness
the vessel's use is its hollow

s: 'form is emptiness' means nothing really exists
the cup is there: that's form. empty means empty of a separate self, made of everything else.
in the longer telling, the Buddha approves Avalokiteshvara's answer
he rises from meditation and says: well said, well said.
the Heart Sutra and the Tao Te Ching mean the same thing by empty
the Tao Te Ching's empty is the useful hollow; the sutra's is the cup itself, lacking a separate self.

games.q: a friend is crushed: she thinks her failed exam proves she's 'just a failure.' what would the Heart Sutra's teaching say?
o: that label has no self of its own; it's made of causes, and causes change.
nothing is real, so the exam and her feelings don't matter.
empty your mind of the thought and it will disappear.
games.why: empty doesn't mean unreal. it means arising from causes, so nothing, a 'failure' included, is fixed for good.

practice: Take an empty cup and hold it: the shape, the weight, the hollow. Fill it with water, slowly, and then drink a little.
While you do, name to yourself a few of the things this moment is made of: the cup, the water, the pipe, the rain, your hand.

wordCard.voice: Form and emptiness: the Heart Sutra's center. Form is emptiness, emptiness is form, rupam shunyata in the Sanskrit.

orig.note: Sanskrit, the Heart Sutra: form is emptiness, emptiness itself is form.

carryVoice: Your line: form is emptiness, and the cup is still in your hand. One more day of the Heart Sutra.

sources.ref: Heart Sutra (form is emptiness, emptiness is form; emptiness is not other than form; the longer version's frame on Vulture Peak, with the Buddha's 'well said')

sources.q: Clay is fashioned into vessels; but it is on their empty hollowness, that their use depends.

sources.ref: Thich Nhat Hanh, The Heart of Understanding (a sheet of paper holds the cloud), paraphrased
